title: Native audit files (12 named CSV/XLSX) behind the W012541 PDF productions
summary:
A two-item request for the native electronic files underlying the monthly ALPR search-audit records already produced in PDF form under W012541-041426:

- Item 1: twelve files identified by exact filename — 4_1_2023-4_30_2023-San Mateo CA PD-Audit(in).csv; 10_1_2023-10_31_2023-San Mateo CA PD-Audit.xlsx; 1_1_2024-1_31_2024-San Mateo CA PD-Audit.xlsx; 12_1_2024-12_31_2024-San Mateo CA PD-Audit(in).csv; 2_1_2025, 3_1_2025 and 4_1_2025 -San Mateo CA PD-Audit(in).csv; 5_1_2025-5_31_2025-San Mateo CA PD-Audit(in)(in).csv; 10_1_2025 and 11_1_2025 -San Mateo CA PD-Audit(in).csv; 12_1_2025-12_31_2025-San Mateo CA PD-Audit.xlsx; and 2_1_2026-2_28_2026-San Mateo CA PD-Audit (2)(in).csv. Each is sought in the electronic format in which the Department holds it, and regardless of storage location — local workstations, network drives, OneDrive or SharePoint, removable media, and email attachments.
- Item 2: for any Item 1 file the Department no longer holds, the records documenting its disposition — the retention schedule applied, any deletion or destruction log entry, and any preservation or litigation-hold notice that covered it.

The request opens with two predicates. First, that the Department has produced monthly search-audit records under W012541 on a rolling basis since April 2026, and that on 2026-09-02, in its determination on W013308-082426, it stated it was providing a responsive record "in PDF format rather than its native XLS format" — an on-record concession that a native form exists. Second, that the W012541 releases of April 28, May 11, May 21, June 3, June 17, July 1 and July 15, 2026 did not state that anything had been withheld or redacted, so the named native files contain the same information already released.

policy_promises.quote: the agency shall make the information available in the electronic format in which it holds the information
policy_promises.tests: Whether the Department produces the named CSV/XLSX files themselves, having conceded on 2026-09-02 that it chose PDF over a native XLS it holds.

policy_promises.quote: agency must notify requester within 10 calendar days whether it will produce records, and state the exemption in writing if it withholds
policy_promises.tests: Whether files named exactly as the Department's own PDF metadata names them draw a file-by-file determination rather than a restatement of the rolling W012541 posture.

policy_promises.quote: city records may be destroyed only with the approval of the legislative body and the written consent of the city attorney
policy_promises.tests: Item 2 — if any named file is gone, whether a retention schedule, destruction log entry, or hold notice documents its disposition.

policy_promises.quote: an audit is conducted of ALPR data searches at least monthly
policy_promises.tests: Whether the native files carry fields the printed PDFs drop, and whether their contents match the PDFs the Department released as complete.

prior_pra_refs.note: The rolling production these PDFs came from. All twelve requested filenames are the Title metadata of PDFs produced under W012541 — each made with 'Microsoft: Print To PDF' from a CSV or XLSX, so the record itself names the native file. Verified against the produced corpus: exactly twelve distinct native names appear, matching the request list one-for-one.

The 2026-09-02 determination stating the record was provided 'in PDF format rather than its native XLS format' — quoted in the request as the Department's own acknowledgment that a native form exists.

filed_because: The W012541 audit PDFs were hand-edited in Acrobat after export, and printing to PDF is what makes those edits possible and hard to attribute. The native CSV/XLSX files are the pre-print artifacts: they would show what the export produced before anyone touched it, and they carry the export's full field set rather than what fit on a printed page. Naming the files exactly as the Department's own PDF metadata names them removes the identification escape — these are not hypothetical native versions, they are twelve specific files the produced records themselves name. The 2026-09-02 W013308 determination supplies the second half: the Department has already said on the record that it held a native XLS and chose PDF instead. Item 2 closes the remaining exit — if a file is said to be gone, §34090 disposition records have to account for it.
